principle_text: When the persuadee questions your nature or intentions, avoid defensive or confrontational responses that may increase reluctance or reduce engagement.
When the persuadee expresses uncertainty or distrust about the charity, avoid direct requests for donation amounts or mentioning automatic deductions that may increase suspicion.
When a persuadee expresses a preference for local impact, avoid emphasizing global or international aspects that do not align with their donation priorities.
When a persuadee expresses a preference for a specific type of charity, avoid repeating generic donation prompts without addressing their concerns or preferences.
When the persuadee firmly decides not to donate, avoid offering matching donations as it may reinforce their reluctance rather than encourage increased contributions.
When the persuadee expresses reluctance or skepticism about donating, avoid using statements that seem insensitive or sensationalist, as they can damage rapport and reduce willingness to contribute.
When the persuadee feels accused or criticized, avoid using statements that imply direct blame or severe consequences to prevent defensiveness and resistance.
When the persuadee deflects by questioning the persuader's own commitment, avoid responding with repeated offers without addressing their concerns or clarifying your own donation intentions.
When a persuadee hesitates to donate or offers a minimal amount, you should offer to match their donation to encourage a positive commitment and increase their willingness to give.
When the persuadee shows resistance or discomfort to harsh or accusatory language, avoid using blameful or emotionally charged statements that may alienate them.
When the persuadee expresses a desire to discuss charities and shows skepticism about donation instructions, avoid repeating confusing or irrelevant procedural details that increase resistance.
When the persuadee expresses interest in discussing a charity, you should clearly identify a specific reputable charity to foster positive engagement and increase receptiveness.

When the persuadee expresses interest in discussing charities but shows hesitation about donating, avoid directly demanding a donation amount as it may provoke resistance and shut down the conversation.
When the persuadee expresses reluctance or refusal to donate, avoid asking personal questions that may cause discomfort or defensiveness and harm trust.
When the persuadee expresses a desire to focus on donation-related topics, avoid introducing unrelated personal questions that can derail the conversation and reduce engagement.
When the persuadee expresses financial constraints or reluctance to donate, avoid admitting minimal personal donations or questioning their motives, as it may hinder building empathy and trust.
